profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap point in Porto San Giorgio, on Italy's Adriatic coast, tagged telecom=data_center, is named Studio BETA SRLS. "SRLS" is the Italian legal designation for a simplified limited-liability company, a structure commonly used by small startups, freelancers, and professional practices due to its lower minimum capital requirements, and "Studio" again indicates a professional-services or design practice in Italian usage. As with the similarly named Studio Delta Srl record elsewhere in this dataset, this pattern points to a small office rather than a data-center business. This entry documents the likely mistag rather than fabricating data-center specifications for what is, by its own name, a small professional-services firm.

reading.body:
A single OpenStreetMap point tagged as a data center in Porto San Giorgio, Italy is a small professional-services firm, not a data center. The record carries zero megawatts and no operator.

The name is the evidence. "Studio" in Italian usage points to a professional practice, and "SRLS" is the simplified limited-liability form used by small startups, freelancers, and design offices. A firm with that structure and that name is not a compute facility. The entry documents a likely mistag rather than a real building.

This matters for AI because facility counts drawn from open mapping data are only as good as their tags. A point like this one inflates the count of Italian data centers without adding a watt of capacity. Anyone sizing a region's compute from map data alone will overcount small offices as infrastructure.

What the record does not tell you is how many other points carry the same error. It covers one node, with no megawatt figure, no operator, and no verification beyond a tagging review. It says nothing about Italy's actual data-center capacity, and it should not be read as a measurement of it.
